newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - FACTORS TO WATCH - AUG 14.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - FACTORS TO WATCH - AUG 14.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Philippine stocks on Thursday:
* The equities market is likely to continue its downtrend despite a cut in overnight rates as regional volatility on the currency market still lingers, traders said.

* "The mood appears to be negative. Although overnight rates came down, the rise in reserve requirement also means less liquidity. The foreign exchange market is not yet stable so there will still be some nervousness," said Manuel Goseco, analyst at Dharmala Securities.

* "It's a matter of waiting for the market to hit the bottom. With the cut in the overnight rates and the hike in liquidity reserves, what they gave in one hand, they took in another. There's no bright picture for the equities," said Noel Reyes, vice-president at Anscor-Hagedorn Securities.
* On Wednesday, the Philippine composite index closed lower for the fifth straight day by 8.32 points at 2,527.08 points.
* The Dow Jones on Wednesday ended 32.52 points down at 7,928.32. PLDT's ADR closed lower by $0/05 at $30 1/8
* The Philippine peso ended lower at 29.05 to a U.S. dollar versus 28.66.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was steady at 18.0625 percent.

* The central bank said on Wednesday it is cutting its closely-watched overnight borrowing rate to 14 percent from 18 percent effective Thursday. The central bank also raised banks' liquidity reserves on deposits and trust funds to five percent from four percent.
* The newly beleaguered Singapore dollar could be in for a spell of sustained weakness if the U.S. dollar stays bullish internationally and turmoil in Asian currency market persists, economists said.
* Solid Group Inc said it posted 355.99 million peso net income for the first six months of the year compared with 295 million a year ago.
* Central Azucarera de Tarlac have voted to strike, the sugar miller said. The workers were protesting against a retrenchment programme which had laid off more than 500 workers.
* China Banking Corp said its first six months net income rose 513 million pesos to 425 million.
* Aboitiz Equity Ventures Inc said it made 528 million pesos for the first half of the year from 576 million a year ago.
* Republic Resources and Development Co said it had signed an agreement with Hong Kong-based Lucky Seven Overseas Co to form a cigarette making company in the Philippines.

* First-half results from Philippine property firms show profit growth slowing from last year's dizzying heights and analysts on Wednesday said high interest rates should keep the sector under pressure.
